messages.text: McDermott blasts 'harsh' RL World Cup format | 'Lewis has shown humility'

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am) in their second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; Coach Brian McDermott discussed World Cup format and Mikey Lewis' continued absence ahead of weekend clash Thursday 22 October 2026 12:45, UK Image: England coach Brian McDermott has branded the Rugby League World Cup format 'harsh,' with his side up against it to progress England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress. Last Saturday's loss to Tonga means England must hope Tonga beat Samoa in their final group game next week in order to stand any realistic chance of reaching the semi-finals. That scenario would leave England and Samoa to be separated by points difference - a particularly tough ask for McDermott's men given the Samoans started their campaign with a crushing 78-4 win over France. "The jeopardy is losing one game is so harsh, it's almost like we don't get another chance to straighten things out," said McDermott, whose side face the French in their second group game in Perth on Saturday. messages.text: How will Arsenal cope without Saka?

metadata.summary: An innocuous swing of his left boot, a "sharp pain" in his quadriceps, and now an anxious wait for Arsenal. Bukayo Saka's injury was a blot on a positive night against Bayern Munich.
metadata.content: How will Arsenal cope without injured Bukayo Saka? Noni Madueke and Max Dowman in frame for more minutes | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis How will Arsenal cope without injured Bukayo Saka? Noni Madueke and Max Dowman in frame for more minutes Bukayo Saka could face a spell on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, so who will step up in his absence? Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Thursday 22 October 2026 13:03, UK Image: Bukayo Saka limped off early in Arsenal's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich An innocuous swing of his left boot, a "sharp pain" in his quadriceps, and now an anxious wait for Arsenal. Bukayo Saka's injury was a blot on a positive night against Bayern Munich. Mikel Arteta offered a gloomy initial prognosis after his 10th-minute withdrawal, revealing his medical staff were "concerned" and adding that it "doesn't look good at all" in his press conference. The injury is the latest in a string of setbacks for Saka, who was almost always available between 2020/21 and 2023/24 but has struggled with hamstring, Achilles and hip issues since. It also ruptured open divisions in the camp, with club captain Bruno Fernandes criticising the tactical plan. United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season and that European humbling means they are now seven without a win across all competitions. messages.text: Can McLaren 'up their game' to respond to Red Bull threat?

metadata.summary: McLaren will introduce further upgrades at the United States Grand Prix as they bid to improve their car's performance and stave off a resurgent Red Bull in the standings over the remainder of the season.
metadata.content: United States GP: McLaren with upgrades for Austin race as reigning F1 champions bid to ward off Red Bull threat | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: McLaren with upgrades for Austin race as reigning F1 champions bid to ward off Red Bull threat McLaren bidding to hit back with stronger results across the next triple header after seeing Red Bull close right up on them in Constructors' Championship in fight for third; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin from Friday evening, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 22 October 2026 12:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri make contact during the last lap of the Sprint race at the Singapore Grand Prix. McLaren will introduce further upgrades at the United States Grand Prix as they bid to improve their car's performance and stave off a resurgent Red Bull in the standings over the remainder of the season. The reigning world champions continue to sit third in the Constructors' Championship with six rounds to go but fell into the clutches of fourth-placed Red Bull over the first of the end-of-season triple headers. While McLaren failed to score a podium across that run of races, Red Bull claimed four top-three finishes - including two wins for Max Verstappen - to cut what had been a 76-point deficit to their rivals to just seven points.
